narrative: Material PL1__MC035CB1 displays lumpy, high-volume demand averaging 1,641 units/day with a CV of 0.52, indicating substantial day-to-day variability. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.52, mean 2.35 days), contributing significantly to the combined lead-time-demand uncertainty (sigma_LTD=2,395). The recommended (r,Q) policy raises safety stock from 1,503 to 3,940 units to properly buffer this variability at 95% service level, while consolidating from ~999 small orders/year to ~29 larger orders, yielding 94% cost reduction.
warnings: Order quantity capped from 17552 to 14864 units due to storage capacity constraint (max_storage_units=18804.568).
Unstable lead time (CV=0.52). Supplier reliability improvement would reduce required safety stock.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With lumpy but largely non-zero demand (93.2% active days) and a high daily volume, continuous-review is preferred over periodic-review. The (r,Q) model with EOQ-derived order quantity minimises total ordering plus holding cost while the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity caps the order quantity at 14,864 (from EOQ 17,552). This raises annual ordering frequency from 24 to 29 orders and increases ordering cost by ~$375/year, a minor trade-off. If demand grows, the capacity constraint will bind more tightly and a storage expansion review is advised.
